evidence: The Vietnam Museum of Ethnology, an organization under the Vietnam Academy of Social Sciences, is dedicated to scientific research, collecting, inventorying, preserving, restoring objects and materials related to ethnic groups, organizing exhibitions, performances, and other activities to introduce, disseminate, and educate about the historical and cultural values of ethnic groups both within and outside the country. It also provides research materials on ethnic groups for various sectors and trains researchers, professionals, and managers in ethnographic museum studies.

The Vietnam Museum of Ethnology, an organization under the Vietnam Academy of Social Sciences, is dedicated to scientific research, collecting, inventorying, preserving, restoring objects and materials related to ethnic groups, organizing exhibitions, performances, and other activities to introduce, disseminate, and educate about the historical and cultural values of ethnic groups both within and outside the country. It also provides research materials on ethnic groups for various sectors and trains researchers, professionals, and managers in ethnographic museum studies.

The Dong Truong (Bronze Drum Hall) area features permanent exhibitions spread across two floors, introducing the 54 ethnic groups in Vietnam in a very logical manner. On the first floor, visitors can learn about the 54 ethnic groups through images and their regions of residence.

In 2014 and 2015, the museum showcased photographs of the lives and people of the Central Highlands ethnic minorities taken by French photographer Jean-Marie Duchange in the 1950s. The second floor of the Dong Truong building offers visitors a detailed look at minority ethnic groups in Vietnam, arranged scientifically along the country’s geographical layout, starting from the north, moving through central Vietnam and the Central Highlands, and ending in the south.

In addition to these areas, the museum has administrative zones for research facilities, libraries, and object storage systems. The museum houses over 15,000 cultural artifacts from all 54 ethnic groups in Vietnam, including 42,000 films (with color photos), 2,190 film prints, 273 audio recordings of interviews and music, 373 videos, and 25 CD-ROMs (as of 2000).
